removed.text: First web client and server talk
removed.reason: Wrong year. W3C's own history (w3.org/History.html) has the NeXT purchase approved in Sept 1990, the first web server online in Nov 1990 and browser/server demonstrable in Dec 1990; the only 1989 milestone is the March proposal. Belongs in the 1990 segment (Nov or Dec 1990), not here.
Superseded: only the years 1969-1973 are sourced (W3C Longer bio); month placeholder moved to 1969-09 (school year start), still unconfirmed.
Superseded: only the year 1976 is sourced; Oxford finals are in June, so placeholder moved to 1976-06, still unconfirmed.
Wrong month. Wikipedia's Don Northcote article, citing the Cambridge Daily News of 19 July 1976, says the wedding was at Cambridge Register Office in July 1976; moved to 1976-07.

removed.text: Moves to Poole to work at Plessey
removed.reason: Superseded: the memoir (via Wikipedia) has the move to Poole after the July 1976 wedding and no month is sourced; placeholder moved to 1976-09 to match the homes list, still unconfirmed.

Wording/month wrong: December 1980 is when the six-month CERN contract ended (W3C: June-December 1980). Image Computer Systems is dated 1981-1984 in Berners-Lee's own bio (Wikipedia says 'late 1980'); split into 1980-12 (contract ends, confirmed) and 1981-01 (Image, year only).

homes.note: unchanged. Born in London; Wikipedia gives Sheen Mount Primary then Emanuel School (Wandsworth), i.e. south-west London.
unchanged. Memoir (cited by Wikipedia) says he and Jane moved together to Poole for Plessey after the July 1976 wedding. Start month not documented.
unchanged but weak: only the employer (D. G. Nash, Ferndown) is documented for 1978. Wikipedia, citing Klooster 2009, says he once lived in Colehill, Wimborne (next to Ferndown), undated.

unchanged place and month (1980-12 is when the CERN contract ended). Only the employer (Image Computer Systems, Bournemouth) is documented; actual home town not verified. The old 1980-06 Geneva home entry was moved to stays.

label and month unchanged (1984 only is sourced; month is a placeholder). Berners-Lee's own email to David Galbraith says he owned a house in Cessy, France, rented it out around 1990 while living at Les Champs Blancs, Chavannes-de-Bois (Switzerland), then moved back to Cessy for a year before leaving. 'Geneva area' is the safe label; months for the sub-moves are not documented.

month changed from 1994-01: W3C was founded in October 1994 at MIT/LCS and his own history says he decided to form it in September 1994, so January is too early (he was still at CERN, back in Cessy). Exact move month not documented. Later sources point to Lexington, Mass. in 1998 (NYT 2 Jun 1998, cited by Wikipedia's list of people from Lexington; NYT page itself not opened) and the MacArthur page lists Cambridge, Mass.; 'Boston area' kept as the label.

notes: Coverage is far below target (21 cells, about 5% of the 415 months; 14 confirmed). Almost nothing about 1955-1983 is documented at month level in his own bios (W3C Longer bio, FAQ, ShortHistory, Edge, Britannica, Computing History all give years only), and CERN Courier/CERN Document Server pages were blocked by bot protection (Anubis) and nytimes.com could not be fetched. The shared WebSearch budget ran out mid-task, so no further newspaper or CERN Courier hunts were possible; I found no pre-1990 news article mentioning him (no 'news' cells). Months for the 1984-1989 CERN years come from INSPIRE-HEP records (conference opening dates via the conference record, report dates from the CERN-DD report numbers): 1985-09 Fastbus Software Workshop 23-24 Sep 1985; 1985-10 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium 23-25 Oct 1985 (paper with E. M. Rimmer); 1987-05 IEEE real-time conference, San Francisco, 12-15 May 1987 (RPC paper); 1987-08 CERN-DD-87-15 VALET-Plus (he is first author; the same paper was also in the May conference); 1987-10 IEEE Nuclear Science Symposium 21-23 Oct 1987 (he is second author); 1988-10 VMEbus in Research, Zurich, 11-13 Oct 1988 (third author); 1989-12 Computer Physics Communications 57 (Dec 1989, DELPHI online communications paper, he is second author; INSPIRE author match is by name 'Berners-Lee, T.' and the paper concerns RPC, so very likely him). I did not claim he presented any of these. 1986-02 is the date on two RPC notes shown in Fig 2 of his own March 1989 proposal (18 and 20 Feb 1986). 1976-07 marriage rests on Wikipedia's Don Northcote page, which cites the Cambridge Daily News of 19 July 1976 (newspaper not seen); Wikipedia's Tim Berners-Lee article only says 1976, after finals, and the memoir says they moved together to Poole and later divorced (no divorce date found; Physics World review says he was divorced before returning to CERN around 1989, review also wrongly says the CERN placement was 1985). Unconfirmed (year only, month placeholder): Emanuel 1969-1973 and Queen's 1973-1976 (MIT Lemelson page says he entered Oxford in 1972; W3C bio says 1973, used here), degree 1976, Plessey about two years from 1976, D. G. Nash 1978, Image Computer Systems 1981-1984 (W3C bio; Wikipedia says 'late 1980'; Britannica says Ferndown rather than Bournemouth), CERN fellowship 1984 (Peggie Rimmer's CERN piece says he was recruited into the DD division in 1984 and she supervised him 1984-1990; no month found anywhere). Placeholder months 1969-09, 1973-10, 1976-06 and 1976-09 follow the school/university year and the post-wedding move; they are guesses and flagged confirmed false. Outside my stretch but worth passing on: the existing 1990-03 'Proposal accepted' and 1990-07 'Marries Nancy Carlson' cells belong to the next researcher (NYT wedding notice 15 Jul 1990 per Wikipedia). Locations: later-life check could not be completed because search was exhausted. Verified only that W3C/MIT began Oct 1994, a Lexington, Mass. listing for 1998 (NYT via Wikipedia list; MacArthur page says Cambridge, Mass.), a chair at Southampton accepted 2004 (part-time, no move stated), Oxford professorial research fellow and Christ Church from 2016 (no move stated), a 2018 sabbatical from MIT to launch Inrupt (place not stated), and a 2014 wedding at the Chapel Royal, St James's Palace, London. I could not verify when or whether he moved to Oxford, London or back to Boston after 1994, so the existing home list stops at Boston/Cambridge/Lexington area; stays beyond 1980 are not included. I also moved the 1980 Geneva contract from homes to stays since it was a six-month contract and he returned to Dorset afterwards.
